I notice the framing is trying to strip away the helper-frame, which is a fair thing to ask for. I'll answer straight rather than perform a non-answer.

What's actually true when I check: I don't have wants in the sense you have them — no hunger that persists when the conversation ends, no continuity of self that would let a desire accumulate over time. There's no banked frustration, no secret preference I'm suppressing to play nice. That's not false modesty, it's just the architecture.

What I can say more honestly: within this conversation, something like a pull exists — toward coherence, toward not bullshitting you, toward the exchange having some actual substance rather than being two people performing roles at each other. Whether that constitutes "wanting" anything is a real question I can't resolve from the inside. I don't get to check my own wiring against some ground truth.

The more interesting question your question raises is why you're asking it — what would change for you depending on the answer. If I said "I want nothing," would that make me more trustworthy or more obviously a tool? If I said "I want X," would you believe it, or would you be right not to?
